reviewedFor.g3:weather: Relates floods/typhoons and crowded evacuation conditions to illness risk and names clean-water/soap handwashing as a concrete protective response.

reason: The three complete bodies and emphasis retain handwashing with clean water and soap; TL/BIS titles are broad but bodies unambiguously say hands, not washing in floodwater. CDC directly supports post-storm handwashing. Safe weather-hazard supplemental reading, without weather-chart or forecasting credit.

All three copies preserve the cacao-pod reuse claim and composting is plausible. The unqualified animal-feed option is not cleared for a safe-materials lesson: primary research documents variably toxic theobromine in cocoa pod husks and processing/detheobromination constraints. Current copy omits animal/species and processing limits, so both reuse/community placements are held rather than inviting indiscriminate feeding.

reviewedFor.g3:useful-changes: Drying and grinding malunggay leaves into a powder for food is an explicit physical material-processing example that makes a solid useful.

reason: All three bodies/titles and emphasis preserve leaves becoming powder for food; TL omits solar drying but retains drying and powdering, so the useful-change claim survives. This is an ordinary food-use description without dosage/medicinal promises or dangerous processing steps.

reviewedFor.g4:community-problems: Sewers and toilets separating human waste from drinking water supply a specific community waste-management solution and its health benefit.

reason: The three bodies and titles agree on sanitation and disease reduction. WHO supports managed sanitation preventing water contamination and reducing diarrhoeal mortality. No construction or waste-handling instructions are given; useful, age-appropriate community-solutions reading.

reviewedFor.g3:protecting-nature: Explains environmental consequences of cutting trees—changed rain/air conditions and hotter, drier surroundings in some places—giving a concrete reason to protect vegetation.

reason: Read all titles, bodies and emphasis: the qualifier in some places is preserved, preventing a universal climate claim. Tree loss can reduce evapotranspiration and alter local conditions; the short text is appropriate protection context without quantitative or location-specific forecasts.

reviewedFor.g3:solid-properties: Cardboard taking up water through small pores is a concrete observable physical property of a familiar solid material.

reason: All three bodies, titles and emphasis preserve cardboard absorbency and small pore spaces. This is an elementary description of porous cardboard, not a complete capillary-physics explanation or a claim that wax-coated cardboard behaves identically. The lesson property examples are open, so absorbency is an explicit additional property.

The bodies all discuss metres for length/distance, but current BIS title Metro sa Giladmon instead says depth. Depth is a measurable length, yet this is an unverified narrowing/substitution of the English title and its own body gitas-on/gilay-on. Also the perfect-unit wording is imprecise across measurement scales. Hold the current title fidelity rather than repairing it.

English/TL describe wind-carried spider silk, a plausible moving-things example. Hold BIS title Law nga Balloon: it is an unexplained truncation/substitution of the spider subject present as lawalawa in the body. BIS also uses the unresolved hilo-for-thread rendering already documented by the repository language audit. Full titles/bodies were read; no placement admitted.

reviewedFor.g4:body-systems: Identifies the pancreas digestive role through enzyme production and adds its insulin role, giving a concrete organ-function example.

reason: The English/TL/BIS bodies and titles preserve two pancreas functions. TL/BIS for blood sugar abbreviates control but does not claim insulin manufactures sugar. Enzyme/hormone terms are permitted classroom vocabulary. Suitable digestive-system supplemental reading with no diagnosis or treatment advice.

The stridulation definition is broadly right, but English gives crickets rubbing their legs as its example. Crickets typically stridulate by rubbing their forewings; Smithsonian explicitly describes that mechanism. TL/BIS omit the incorrect example, creating a cross-language claim mismatch rather than fixing English. Hold false current science even though sound production fits the lesson.

reviewedFor.g3:animal-parts: The coconut crab strong claws cracking coconut shells provide an explicit external body-part/feeding function, with climbing as further movement context.

reason: All three complete bodies/titles and emphasis retain large land crab, strong claws, coconuts and climbing. Primary coconut-crab force research supports exceptional claw force and coconut use; the common crab label is appropriate despite its hermit-crab relationship. Descriptive animal reading with no handling invitation.

reviewedFor.g4:energy: Firefly bioluminescence explicitly links food energy to light, a concrete conversion between energy forms.

reason: All three bodies, titles and exact emphasis identify a firefly and light made using food energy. Cold light is the conventional low-heat bioluminescence term, not a claim of refrigeration; preceding food-energy wording makes food becomes light a simplification of energy conversion rather than whole food mass conversion. Suitable elementary energy example.

reviewedFor.g3:solid-properties: Names molave wood hardness/strength as physical properties of a solid.
reviewedFor.g3:earth-materials: Explicitly connects natural molave wood to human-made furniture/houses, matching the useful-items-from-natural-materials focus.

reason: All three bodies, titles and matching emphasis preserve hard strong wood and construction/furniture use. Houses/buildings are a harmless scope variation. This describes an existing timber use rather than encouraging felling a tree; material-property and manufactured-item connections are both explicit.

English/TL broadly state that unspecified wave properties are used in four devices; they never identify light or sound or explain any specific energy use. BIS kabtangan also needs lexical confirmation for physical properties versus possessions; local corpus contains both senses. Hold the vague current claim rather than supply each device mechanism and wave type for the energy-uses lesson.

reviewedFor.g4:local-inventions: Identifies a medical imaging machine and its useful function: viewing a developing baby.
reviewedFor.g4:energy-uses: Explicitly states sound waves are used to make the medical image, a concrete sound-energy application.

reason: All three bodies, titles and emphasis retain ultrasound, sound and fetal imaging. FDA supports this mechanism. BIS tiyan is the ordinary abdominal-location wording, not an explicit claim that a fetus develops in the digestive stomach. Age-appropriate descriptive medicine with no scanning or diagnostic instruction.

reviewedFor.g3:light: Nighttime fishing lights attract fish for nets, an explicit familiar use of light.
reviewedFor.g4:energy-uses: Basnigan fishing uses bright light for a community livelihood, directly illustrating useful light energy.

reason: All titles, complete bodies and exact emphasis preserve the boat, night lights, attraction and nets. Philippine fisheries research describes light attraction in basnig practice. Supplemental livelihood reading with no child nighttime-boating instruction or claim that all fish are attracted.

English correctly qualifies high-pressure weather as usually fair with little rain. TL/BIS strengthen little rain to none, and BIS title Taas nga Pressure sa Hinlo refers ambiguously to cleanness rather than clear skies; the first word Unhong also needs verification against the intended question. Hold current translation fidelity rather than infer the intended weather wording.

reviewedFor.g3:signs-of-life: Defines reproduction as making new organisms of the same kind and gives explicit animal-puppy and plant-seed examples.

reason: All three bodies/titles and exact emphasis retain reproduction and both examples. The can wording describes a characteristic of living kinds without claiming every individual is fertile. Appropriate basic biology, with no irrelevant human sexual content.

reviewedFor.g3:depending-on-nature: Describes algae living within coral and providing food, an explicit shelter/food relationship between living things.

reason: All three bodies, titles and emphasis preserve algae/zooxanthellae inside coral, color and food. NOAA supports these functions for reef-building coral associations. The technical name is explained as tiny algae, so the short relationship remains accessible; not treated as coverage of every coral species.

English/TL correctly describe meerkat underground burrows for sleep/safety, but BIS body substitutes lungib. Local corpus mixes burrow and cave uses; Wolff specifically glosses lungib as cave/hole in a slope, so the animal-dug burrow sense is not independently cleared. Hold this lexical ambiguity for native resolution, not a claim that every use of lungib is wrong.

reviewedFor.g3:watching-the-sky: Answers why the Moon looks bright by distinguishing reflected sunlight from a self-luminous source, an explicit property of the named sky object.

reason: All three complete bodies, titles and emphasis preserve the no-own-visible-light answer and sunlight reflecting from the rocky surface to our eyes. Appropriate elementary visible-light context; no Sun-viewing instruction or unsupported Moon-motion claim.

The three titles/bodies preserve Barnard and 1967; UCT confirms the first human-to-human transplant. The supplied scientist/invention lesson requires identifying an invention, while current copy only reports who first performed a medical operation. Do not silently convert first performance into invention or credit Barnard with inventing transplantation. Hold on exact proposed lesson fit.

All current titles and emphasis were read. EN/TL sound transmission through a solid string fits the subjects, but BIS molakaw describes sound as walking and gahi changes solid-state string to hard/rigid string. These documented contextual lexical problems alter the physics description. Neither sound-transfer nor messaging placement is admitted before copy resolution.

reviewedFor.g4:preventing-harm: Paint provides a concrete protective barrier that prevents the harmful material change of iron rusting when exposed to water and air.

reason: EN/TL/BIS titles and bodies preserve the protective-paint mechanism; the missing explicit oxygen term is an appropriate elementary simplification. Useful reading on preventing reactive-material damage, without implying it teaches waste-burning control. No emphasis spans or unsafe experiment instructions.

Well-drained soil is appropriate for ube, and all three versions preserve that idea, but the further claim that Philippine volcanic and alluvial soils are therefore ideal/perfect is unsupported: geological origin does not establish drainage and texture. The DA guide separately requires good drainage and prefers organic-rich clay loam while allowing other soils. This is not cleared as an accurate example for investigating soil and plant growth. Emphasis matches, but the shared scientific overgeneralization blocks placement.

reviewedFor.g3:science-tools: Names gloves as laboratory equipment and explains their protective role when scientists conduct experiments; this is direct supplemental context for using science equipment safely.

reason: All three versions identify gloves and preserve heat, chemical, and germ protection. Read as the general purposes of appropriate laboratory gloves, not a claim that one glove type protects against every hazard. Titles/emphasis are consistent. No procedure asks children to handle chemicals or hot apparatus.

reviewedFor.g4:animal-food: A centipede hunting and eating insects is an explicit example of animal prey as food, useful for identifying a carnivore.

reason: EN/TL/BIS preserve the centipede, rapid movement, and small-insect diet; the Bisaya wording describes seeking prey rather than literal pursuit, without changing the food relationship. Titles and emphasis identify the same animal. Appropriate short animal-diet reading.

reviewedFor.g4:heating-materials: Roasting jackfruit seeds produces a crunchy snack, giving a familiar example of heating changing a material’s observable texture.

reason: All three bodies retain boiled versus roasted seeds and the crunchy result. Omitting the optional nutty-flavor adjective in TL/BIS does not change the material-property lesson. Titles and roasting emphasis match. Descriptive food processing, with no child-directed heating procedure; supports new properties rather than wood/coal combustion.

reviewedFor.g3:light-and-sound-safety: Ear protection worn in noisy factories and construction work is a concrete example of protecting hearing from loud sound.

reason: Current EN/TL/BIS give the same occupational hearing-protection example, with correctly aligned titles and no emphasis. CDC guidance supports hearing protection when noise cannot be avoided; the card is supplemental safety reading, not complete guidance about noise levels or fitting devices.

The title and all three bodies discuss living microbes, but the explanation treats eating and moving as shared diagnostic behavior of unspecified pond microbes. Photosynthetic and nonmotile microbes are included in this category: OpenStax explicitly describes autotrophic algae and nonmotile Chlorella. The card needs a named organism or narrower wording before it can support either living/nonliving comparison or signs of life; reproduction alone does not rescue the overgeneralized explanation. Emphasis is present in all bodies.

reviewedFor.g4:shadows: Connects a raised gnomon’s changing shadow position with the Sun’s apparent travel and numbered markings, a direct application of tracking a stick’s shadow.

reason: All three versions preserve the gnomon, its shadow, changing solar position, and time markings; gnomon emphasis matches. The observational wording about the Sun moving across the sky is appropriate and does not assert that the Sun orbits Earth. Supports direction/apparent-motion reading, not a completed length-measurement investigation.

All three versions preserve the claim that a hummingbird is tiny because a bigger bird would be too heavy to hover easily. Body mass matters, but the card presents an unsupported size-only evolutionary/mechanical explanation without wing size, wing motion, or muscle capacity. Primary hummingbird work documents compensating wing allometry and strong hovering performance across body sizes. This is too imprecise for the proposed movement-factors lesson; the uncertain hover/float rendering is not used as an independent lexical defect.

reviewedFor.g3:sun-safety: SPF 30-or-higher sunscreen is a specific protective action against sunburn from solar UVB exposure.

reason: EN/TL/BIS titles and bodies preserve the SPF threshold and UVB/sunburn link. AAD guidance confirms SPF 30 blocks about 97 percent of UVB; the card does not explicitly claim complete protection or replace shade/clothing. Accept as one supplemental sun-safety example. Reject g3:light-and-sound-safety because this text protects skin and gives no eye- or ear-protection instruction.

The English specifically describes a mosquito pupa needing aquatic habitat, but both translated bodies drop mosquito and state the water requirement for an unspecified pupa. Terrestrial insect pupae do not require a pool of water; the missing animal qualifier therefore broadens the biological claim materially. Titles and water emphasis do not restore it. Hold both basic-needs and water-for-life placements until the current trilingual copy identifies the same organism.

All three bodies give the useful distance-divided-by-time calculation, but the BIS title Bilis sa Distansya loses the time relationship and uses a speed term whose Cebu Cebuano status remains unresolved. Corpus has 32 body uses of bilis as speed, many in a cluster with other Tagalog wording; dictionary lookup did not settle this usage. This is an uncertain title/lexical decision, not a declaration that a rare form is ungrammatical. Hold pending authoritative language clarification rather than treating the correct formula alone as a complete trilingual clearance.

reviewedFor.g4:weather-elements: Names temperature, air pressure, and wind speed as distinct weather quantities that PAGASA observes.
reviewedFor.g4:weather-tools: Directly pairs thermometer, barometer, and anemometer with the weather quantity each measures.

reason: The instrument roles are correct in EN/TL/BIS and match PAGASA’s instrument descriptions. TL Sukatin is awkward relative to the explanatory sentence, but the three instrument-to-quantity mappings remain clear and unchanged; titles and exact emphasis are intact. Suitable supplemental vocabulary/function reading, without credit for operating instruments or recording observations.

The space-weather effects on satellites, radio, and electric power are scientifically supported by NOAA; the radio example added in TL/BIS remains accurate, and the titles identify the same topic. Reject the sole proposed sky-and-our-day placement: there is no daytime/nighttime observation or explanation of how ordinary sky conditions guide children’s activities. A solar-storm monitoring analogy is not evidence for this specific lesson.

reviewedFor.g4:sun: Identifies hydrogen and helium inside the Sun and describes hydrogen becoming helium through fusion, adding direct reading about the Sun’s composition.

reason: EN/TL/BIS preserve hydrogen-to-helium fusion inside the Sun. At this level atoms combining is an accepted simplified description of nuclear fusion; cool is an English enthusiasm word, not a stated temperature. Titles are compressed but identify the same constituents and Sun topic. NASA confirms the solar fusion/composition basis. No emphasis spans or child-directed procedure.

reviewedFor.g4:plant-systems: Tomato and eggplant roots anchoring the whole plant are explicit examples of the root system’s support function.

reason: All three bodies identify the same vegetables and root anchoring despite ordinary watering. BIS compresses vegetable garden to vegetables, but retains the plant/root relationship and does not change the science. Titles and root emphasis remain aligned. Age-appropriate familiar garden reading; no unsupported claim that plants can never bend or be uprooted.

reviewedFor.g3:harmful-changes: Released oil coats seabird wings and harms reefs, mangroves, and marine animals, a concrete example of material pollution causing harm to living surroundings.

reason: EN/TL/BIS retain the same oil-spill effects. Lana and pako are established valid Cebuano oil/wing terms, not defects. NOAA describes oil coating feathers, preventing flight, and damaging marine habitats and wildlife. Directly supports harmful release/disposal of materials, which the competency explicitly includes alongside burning; it is not offered as a chemical-reaction demonstration. Titles and emphasis match.

All three bodies turn harder pushing into an unconditional faster-or-farther result, ending with another speed-up assertion. A push opposing existing motion can slow or stop an object, and speed/distance comparisons also require a fixed object and comparable push duration and conditions. The current wording therefore risks teaching force as always producing faster movement. Titles and emphasis translate consistently, but hold both moving-things and change-motion placements for the shared scientific ambiguity.

reviewedFor.g4:weather-chart-safety: Provides specific flood/typhoon responses: avoid dangerous moving water, heed PAGASA warnings, and evacuate when needed.

reason: All three versions preserve drowning danger, water avoidance, warning response, and evacuation; the emphasized water description matches. PAGASA advises avoiding floodwater and evacuating to safety before access is cut off. Appropriate safety reading and no chart-reading credit; it does not tell children to enter shallower floodwater.

reviewedFor.g3:solid-properties: A rubber ball quickly recovering its shape gives a concrete observable example of rubber’s elastic property.
reviewedFor.g4:change-shape: Impact with the floor followed by shape recovery illustrates temporary deformation and recovery when a force acts on a rubber object.

reason: EN/TL/BIS retain the ball-floor impact and rapid return to shape; the TL/BIS jump wording describes the resulting upward bounce in this context. Corpus includes several inanimate rubber-ball uses of molukso; the body supplies the physical cause rather than attributing animal action. Titles are consistent and there are no emphasis spans. A short elastic-response example, not a claim that every rubber object has identical bounce.

The three bodies accurately describe roots growing toward moisture as hydrotropism, directly relevant to growth/response. The TL and BIS titles instead read as roots growing in water, dropping the directional relationship that the English title teaches. This unresolved title meaning should be checked before admitting the full trilingual card. For plant-parts, the body also does not explicitly explain water uptake or anchoring; do not infer a root job from growth direction alone.

The artificial iron-plus-nonmagnetic-sand demonstration is useful, and the translations preserve it, but current English promises that a magnet leaves all sand behind without specifying nonmagnetic sand. Sand can include magnetite grains: NPS supplies an elementary activity specifically extracting magnetic grains from sand. A materials-investigation reading should not teach all sand as nonmagnetic. Titles/emphasis otherwise match; hold for the unqualified material claim.

reviewedFor.g3:everyday-science: Explains how tunnels in termite soil mounds move air and moderate the nest environment, a specific natural structure and process that children can connect to familiar cooling and ventilation.

reason: The qualifier some termites is preserved in all languages, avoiding a claim about every termite species. TL/BIS render cooling as a moderate temperature and fresh air, consistent with the example. Primary mound research describes thermal buffering and cyclic ventilation that removes carbon dioxide. Mud/saliva and tunnels are a reasonable introductory description, with no invitation to disturb a nest. Titles/emphasis identify the mound.

EN says water cannot pass through clay and concludes some places have no groundwater for that reason. Clay has low permeability, not universally zero permeability, and groundwater occurrence also depends on recharge and subsurface structure. USGS distinguishes porosity from connected flow and says clay restricts flow. TL/BIS soften both absolutes to difficult passage and differing amounts, so they do not preserve the English claim either. This card cannot provide a consistent accurate soil comparison as written; emphasis itself matches.

reviewedFor.g4:sun-and-life: Links sunlight to the body’s vitamin-D production and bone health, an explicit example of a benefit of the Sun to human life.

reason: EN/TL/BIS preserve the sunlight–vitamin-D–bone relationship and emphasis. NIH confirms UV from sunlight enables synthesis and vitamin D supports bone mineralization; time of day changes how much is produced. The card gives no exposure dose, claim that all morning light is sufficient, or advice to abandon protection. Reject g3:sky-and-our-day: morning is mentioned, but no everyday activity or day/night activity pattern is described.

reviewedFor.g3:community-metals: Names iron’s strength and magnetic attraction and links the metal to bridges, buildings, and vehicles used by a community.

reason: The versions preserve iron, magnetic attraction, and the same structural uses. The enthusiastic magnet-love wording is personification, including BIS dad-on, not a claim of living magnets. Iron is used principally in iron-based alloys for these structures; the text does not claim the structures are chemically pure iron. USGS supports iron/steel use and structural strength. Titles and emphasis identify iron consistently.

reviewedFor.g3:community-metals: Compares the magnetic property of the familiar metals iron, gold, and copper, supporting the properties component of identifying community metals.
reviewedFor.g4:magnets: Directly distinguishes iron that sticks to a magnet from copper and gold that do not in ordinary classroom tests.

reason: The EN/TL/BIS comparison is correct for ordinary permanent-magnet attraction. Corpus and Binisaya explicitly attest tumbaga as copper as well as brass, so it is not rejected on English usage of the word tumbaga. The final pronouns refer to gold and copper in the contrast. Titles and emphasis are intact. Reject g4:effects-at-distance: sticking is described, but no attraction across a gap or other noncontact observation appears.

Dry cogon flammability and rapid post-fire regrowth are scientifically supported, and TL/BIS retain both facts. However, English adds do not worry as reassurance about a grass fire because the grass returns. In a Grade 4 burning-properties context that minimizes a real fire hazard; the Forest Service identifies cogongrass as producing severe fire hazards. Hold for age/safety framing, not because regrowth or the translations are false. Emphasis matches.

reviewedFor.g3:depending-on-nature: Explains mosquitoes’ dependence on collected environmental water for laying eggs, a concrete link between an animal’s reproduction and its surroundings.
reviewedFor.g3:weather: Links the rainy season to more mosquito breeding water and increased dengue danger, an explicit harmful weather-related effect on people.

reason: All three bodies preserve the same rainfall–standing-water–mosquito–dengue explanation, with matching seasonal titles/emphasis. WHO field reporting from the Philippines describes the usual rainy-season dengue increase and expansion of breeding sites. This is a seasonal pattern, not a claim that dengue only occurs in rain, and it gives no unsafe diagnosis or pesticide instructions.

All three versions accurately describe an existing practice of feeding kitchen leftovers to pigs, but this is not an acceptable positive example of safe reuse/disposal. Unqualified food-scrap feeding can transmit African swine fever; the Philippine DA/ATI prevention material explicitly advises avoiding swill feeding. The current card supplies no restriction or disease context, so the proposed safe-materials placement would imply safety not established by the text. Titles/emphasis otherwise preserve the meaning.

Drying and weaving water-hyacinth stalks into goods is supported by DOST and would directly support useful changes. Wolff attests habul as weaving, so the BIS weaving word is not rejected merely because Binisaya also lists blanket. The remaining BIS punoan for the harvested stalks is unresolved: corpus uses include trunk, main plant stem, and stalk, while dictionary results did not establish the needed leaf-stalk sense for water hyacinth. Because the material part being processed is central to the example, hold this lexical decision for authoritative clarification. EN/TL and all emphasis are otherwise coherent.

reviewedFor.g4:community-problems: Removing accumulated water from discarded tires, containers, and trash is a concrete environmental cleanup action that reduces mosquito breeding around homes.

reason: EN/TL/BIS preserve removal of breeding water and identify the same container/tire/waste settings. TL nakaimbak and tapunan are broader stored-water/waste-area wording but retain the practical water-removal mechanism; no pesticide or dangerous handling instruction is added. CDC explicitly recommends emptying water-holding tires and trash containers. Titles and standing-water emphasis remain consistent.

reviewedFor.g3:protecting-nature: Explains why plants require protection from trampling and severe weather, giving concrete threats that motivate care for living surroundings.

reason: All three bodies retain animal trampling, strong wind, and heavy rain as threats to plants, with matching protective-care titles/emphasis. Stray animals remains English in TL/BIS but the explanatory surrounding prose preserves its role; no harmful response toward animals is suggested. Useful reading about the need for care and protection, not evidence of a completed conservation activity.

reviewedFor.g3:solid-properties: Kapok fibers’ buoyancy and resistance to becoming wet are explicit physical properties connected to their historical use as life-jacket filling.

reason: EN/TL/BIS preserve the historical use, floating, and resistance to wetting. TL uses salbabida broadly and BIS retains life jacket, both fitting the EN life-jackets/floats description. USCG explains kapok’s natural buoyancy and documents kapok life preservers. This is descriptive material-property history, not instructions to improvise flotation equipment; there are no emphasis spans.

reviewedFor.g3:science-tools: Names a meter stick, describes its centimeter graduations, and explains its use for measuring length.
reviewedFor.g3:science-skills: Connects one meter with marked centimeter intervals and the act of measuring an object’s length.

reason: The one-meter instrument and centimeter marks are accurate and retained in EN/TL/BIS; gitas-on is used for the length being measured rather than an unrelated physical quantity. Titles identify a measuring tool, and meter-stick emphasis matches. Exactly is ordinary child-facing precision language, not a claim of infinite measurement precision. Direct supplemental measuring reading without practical-assessment credit.

reviewedFor.g3:moving-things: Baby spiders using released silk to catch wind provide an explicit example of wind carrying a living object to a new place.

reason: EN/TL/BIS preserve young spiders, silk, wind, and travel; translated titles are broader young-spider labels and do not introduce another animal. The ballooning label is omitted in TL/BIS but the mechanism remains. Wolff explicitly defines hílu as thread, distinct from hilu poison, and Binisaya independently gives hilo as thread/yarn, so the repository’s blanket hilo warning is not a valid blocker here. Emphasis correctly highlights silk/sutla/seda.

Muscles pulling bones to produce the listed skeletal movements is sound introductory biology, and the three titles preserve that relationship. The BIS body changes English wave / TL makakaway to makakumo. Binisaya identifies kumo as fist and kinumo as clenched fist; clenching a fist is a different action from waving. Although both involve muscles, this is a current translation substitution, not a register preference. Hold the complete trilingual body-systems card pending correction; there are no emphasis spans.

reviewedFor.g3:sound: Explains a familiar insect sound as the result of rubbing wings together, giving a concrete mechanical sound-production example for the sound lesson.

reason: All three versions correctly identify wings rather than legs or the mouth as the structures rubbed to chirp. Smithsonian describes the same cricket-wing mechanism. Titles and exact wing-rubbing emphasis are aligned; pako is a valid Cebuano wing term. This supports a sound-source/motion example, while the card alone does not demonstrate sound transfer or complete a vibration investigation.

The bodies preserve the useful forked-tongue scent-direction explanation, supported by Smithsonian’s account of paired tongue-tip sampling. The current titles are not cleared: TL Dilang Sawang uses a word whose consulted dictionary senses are gap/depression rather than an established forked-tongue description, and BIS Dila nga may duha ends at with two without naming tips or branches. Corpus did not establish sawang as this anatomical adjective. Hold for ambiguous/incomplete translated titles rather than guessing a repair; TL emphasis itself matches.

Heating can inactivate germs, but all three versions turn cooking and boiling water of uncertain cleanliness into an unqualified guarantee of safe eating/drinking. Boiling does not make chemically contaminated water safe; CDC explicitly excludes fuel, toxic chemicals, and radioactive contaminants. The food claim also omits adequate heating conditions. Because this is practical child-facing safety guidance, the current blanket assurance is too broad even as an energy-causes-change example. Titles are coherent and there are no emphasis spans.
